lunar_base.name: Lunar surface base
lunar_base.source: Light travel time over the mean Earth–Moon distance (~384,400 km / c ≈ 1.28 s); NASA ASCEND paper describes few-second maximum delays just beyond the Moon. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20220013418/downloads/ASCEND-Communication%20Delays%2C%20Disruptions%2C%20and%20Blackouts%20for%20Crewed%20Mars%20Missions.pdf

mars_transit.name: Mars transit
mars_transit.source: NASA ASCEND paper: Earth–Mars one-way delays vary from 0 to 22 minutes over a mission. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20220013418/downloads/ASCEND-Communication%20Delays%2C%20Disruptions%2C%20and%20Blackouts%20for%20Crewed%20Mars%20Missions.pdf

mars_rover.name: Mars surface rover
mars_rover.source: NASA ASCEND paper: Earth–Mars one-way delays vary from 0 to 22 minutes over a mission (a pressurized rover on Mars reaches Earth through the surface base or an orbiter; that relay is a team assumption). https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20220013418/downloads/ASCEND-Communication%20Delays%2C%20Disruptions%2C%20and%20Blackouts%20for%20Crewed%20Mars%20Missions.pdf
